name: E-Commerce Sales
description: Basic e-commerce database with customer orders and product catalog. Ideal for learning JOINs and aggregate functions.

tables.name: customers
tables.description: Customer master data including membership tier and location

tables.name: products
tables.description: Product catalog with pricing and inventory stock levels

tables.name: orders
tables.description: Order transactions linking customers to products with payment and shipping details

relationships.description: Each order belongs to one customer

sample_queries.title: Top 10 Customers by Total Revenue
sample_queries.description: Find customers with highest total order value across all transactions
sample_queries.sql:
SELECT 
  c.customer_name,
  c.city,
  c.membership_tier,
  COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders,
  SUM(o.total_amount) as total_revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.city, c.membership_tier
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10;

sample_queries.title: Monthly Sales Trend
sample_queries.description: Sales volume and revenue aggregated by month
sample_queries.sql:
SELECT 
  DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) as month,
  COUNT(*) as order_count,
  SUM(total_amount) as total_sales,
  AVG(total_amount) as avg_order_value
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

sample_queries.title: Product Performance by Category
sample_queries.description: Sales metrics grouped by product category
sample_queries.sql:
SELECT 
  p.category,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) as orders,
  SUM(o.quantity) as units_sold,
  SUM(o.total_amount) as revenue,
  AVG(p.stock) as avg_stock_level
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN orders o ON p.product_id = o.product_id
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
